questions.question: Branding is just about having a logo and a catchy slogan.
questions.answer: False - Branding goes far beyond logos and slogans. It encompasses a company's identity, values, tone, customer experience, and emotional connection with its audience.

questions.question: Only large companies need to worry about branding.
questions.answer: False - Branding is important for businesses of all sizes. Even small companies and individuals benefit from a clear, consistent brand identity that builds trust and recognition.

questions.question: A strong product will sell itself—branding is unnecessary.
questions.answer: False - While product quality is crucial, branding plays a key role in how a product is perceived, remembered, and differentiated from competitors.

questions.question: Once you’ve created a brand, it should never change.
questions.answer: False - Brands evolve over time to stay relevant, respond to market changes, and reflect updated values or audiences. Rebranding can be a strategic move.

questions.question: Branding is only important for consumer-facing companies.
questions.answer: False - Business-to-business (B2B) companies also benefit from strong branding, which helps build trust, credibility, and loyalty with clients and partners.

questions.question: A good logo guarantees a successful brand.
questions.answer: False - A logo is just one part of a brand. Successful branding also requires strategy, storytelling, consistent messaging, and a strong customer experience.

questions.question: Branding is a one-time project done during a company launch.
questions.answer: False - Branding is an ongoing effort. It must be maintained and reinforced across all touchpoints to ensure consistency and relevance.

questions.question: Your brand is what you say it is.
questions.answer: False - Your brand is ultimately defined by how your audience perceives you. Branding efforts help influence that perception, but it’s shaped through experience and reputation.

questions.question: Visual consistency is more important than emotional impact in branding.
questions.answer: False - Both are important, but emotional connection often drives loyalty and long-term success. A brand that resonates emotionally creates stronger relationships.

questions.question: You don’t need branding if you’re not selling a product.
questions.answer: False - Whether you're selling a product, service, or idea—or building a personal brand—branding helps you stand out and communicate your value clearly.
